 Kyle Shanahan makes shocking admission about player availability for Week 7  
 The San Francisco 49ers have handled business despite injury issues. This week, coach Kyle Shanahan admitted it might be a problem. 
 By Dylan Grausz • 
 Published October 23, 2026 • 
 Updated on October 24, 2026 at 6:13 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 Share 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan speaks to reporters after practice on Friday at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara. 
 The 49ers are decimated with injuries, and it might finally catch up to them.
 Speaking to reporters on Friday, coach Kyle Shanahan ruled out wide receivers Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, defensive lineman Nick Bosa, linebackers Garret Wallow, Luke Gifford and defensive back Marques Sigle for the team's Week 7 game against the Atlanta Falcons.
 With those six players ruled out, Shanahan admitted that San Francisco might not have enough healthy players available, forcing the franchise to dig deep. The NFL allows 48 players per team to be active on game day.

 "It means Rourke and maybe [OL Enrique] Cruz [Jr.],” Shanahan told reporters. “Those would be the two guys that would be our emergency receivers in the game (laughter). No, but that would be the two left.”
 Shanahan has coached in the NFL for a long time and been through a lot over the course of his career. But this injury predicament is something he never has dealt with before.
 "No, I don't think so. I don't think here. I don't think ever in my career, so it's a unique situation," Shanahan told reporters.
 San Francisco goes on its bye week after this game and could get some injured players back. The 49ers desperately want to beat the Falcons, though, and in order for the team to get by, healthy players need to step up in a big way. That means some guys might line up at unfamiliar positions if need be.

 "It's stuff we've talked about throughout the week,” Shanahan told reporters. “Hope it doesn't get to it, and odds are it won't, but it definitely could. You're always a few injuries away from those situations and now it comes down to a couple. So, percentages go up."
 In spite of the injuries, the team is playing at a high level and off to a 6-0 start for the first time since 2019. If they can go into the bye with a win, the 49ers will be set up nicely for a deep playoff push once players such as Evans, Samuel and Bosa return.
